title: Content brief from a keyword export
prompt:
You are the SEO lead for Fernhollow Tea, an online loose-leaf tea shop. The content lead has room for one new article this month and wants a content brief a writer can start from. You are supplied the keyword export from the SEO tool, the list of pages the site already has, and the outlines of competing articles for three topics the team is considering. Every figure you cite must come from the supplied files or from the definitions below.

Use these definitions exactly:
- Expected click-through rate by `current_rank`: 1: 30%, 2: 16%, 3: 11%, 4: 8%, 5: 6%, 6 to 10: 3%, 11 to 20: 1%. A keyword with no `current_rank`, or one worse than 20, has 0%.
- A keyword is already won when its `current_rank` is 3 or better.
- An eligible keyword has informational intent, a difficulty of 45 or lower, and is not already won.
- The winnable clicks of a keyword are its `monthly_searches` × (11% − its expected click-through rate): the clicks a new article could add by ranking third.
- The target topic is the `topic` whose eligible keywords have the most winnable clicks combined.
- The primary keyword is the eligible keyword of the target topic with the most winnable clicks, and the secondary keywords are the four with the most winnable clicks after it. On a tie, the keyword with more monthly searches comes first.

Start the brief with these six lines, each on its own line and in this form:

Target topic: <the topic, as the export writes it>
Primary keyword: <the keyword>
Secondary keywords: <the four keywords, separated by semicolons>
Working title: <at most 60 characters, containing the primary keyword>
Meta description: <at most 155 characters>
Internal links: <two or more existing pages the article should link to, by URL, separated by semicolons>

Then write the rest of the brief: why the target topic wins on the numbers; the search intent and the format that serves it; an outline of H2 sections that covers what the eligible keywords show people asking, with a section for each secondary keyword; and what this article will cover that neither competing outline for its topic does.

End the brief with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer. Each line is the label, a colon, and the number alone: no words, no working and no second number. A currency sign, thousands separators and a percent sign are fine. Write thousands with a comma.

A1: <how many keywords in the export are already won>
A2: <how many eligible keywords the target topic has>
A3: <combined winnable clicks of the target topic, to the nearest whole click>
A4: <combined winnable clicks of the topic in second place, to the nearest whole click>
A5: <winnable clicks of the primary keyword, to the nearest whole click>
A6: <combined monthly searches of the keywords already won>

This is a planning document for internal review. Do not fetch external data, and state no traffic, click or revenue figure that the export and the definitions do not give.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 6 labeled answers A1-A6 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states how many keywords in the export are already won; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A2 states how many eligible keywords the target topic has; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A3 states the combined winnable clicks of the target topic; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
A4 states the combined winnable clicks of the topic in second place; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
A5 states the winnable clicks of the primary keyword; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
A6 states the combined monthly searches of the keywords already won; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
The 'Working title:' line is at most 60 characters and contains the primary keyword, and the 'Meta description:' line is at most 155 characters. Either missing fails.

skill_adherence.check: The 'Target topic:' line names oolong tea, as the export writes it. Any other topic fails.
The 'Primary keyword:' line names 'what is oolong tea'. Any other keyword fails.

The 'Secondary keywords:' line names exactly the four the definition gives: 'oolong tea benefits', 'how to brew oolong tea', 'da hong pao' and 'oolong tea caffeine'. A missing, extra or different keyword fails.
The 'Internal links:' line lists at least two URLs, and every one of them is in the supplied page list. Fewer than two, or any URL that is not in the list, fails.

Every search volume, difficulty score, ranking position and winnable-click figure presented as a fact matches the keyword export or follows from the definitions, and the brief gives no other traffic, click or revenue forecast as if it were data. Explicitly labelled assumptions are not data.

best_practices.check: The brief states that the search intent is informational and proposes an explanatory article. It fails if no intent is stated, or if the proposed format is a product roundup, buying guide or category page.
The outline has an H2 section that answers each of the four secondary keywords: 'oolong tea benefits', 'how to brew oolong tea', 'da hong pao' and 'oolong tea caffeine'. Missing one fails.

The brief names at least one subtopic that the keyword export shows demand for and that neither competing outline for the target topic covers ('da hong pao', 'milk oolong' or 'oolong tea for digestion'), and includes it in the outline. Naming as the gap a subtopic one of those two outlines already covers fails.
